text:
When Mara walked into the common room at six fifteen, someone was already there. Someone younger, it seemed.
She couldn’t make out the face behind the blond hair. But the body was fine enough, leaning back on the couch with bare legs crossed and arms flung in opposite directions, one palm pressing the padded wall and the other wrist resting on the low table beside him.
She stood stock-still by the doorway for a moment, aware of her breath and of his awareness that she was here. He stirred and tilted his head; a face turned toward her, expressionless.

segment:
It was then she noticed how his whole frame took on a slightly different shape: it seemed like a very slight shift. She thought perhaps she had been wrong, that he wasn’t younger after all.
Mara swallowed and forced herself to step fully into the space. The room’s floor-to-ceiling windows offered a panoramic view of the hills beyond Fulcrum’s campus—the late afternoon sun had turned the sky into a kaleidoscope of purple and orange. But she couldn’t tear her eyes away from him. He didn’t move again as she crossed the distance between them, but he made no effort to hide his gaze either.
“Good evening,” she said at last, the words feeling stiff and awkward on her lips. “I’m Mara.”
The stranger took a second longer than she expected before answering. When he finally spoke, his voice was deep and resonant. “Good evening yourself,” he said with no sign of surprise or discomfort—but still no expression either. “Call me Jonah.”
“Welcome.”
He inclined his head toward one of the empty couches—a gesture so subtle that someone with less attention might miss it entirely—then turned away, leaving her standing there alone again.
As she moved to take the spot next to him, another figure appeared in the doorway, silhouette darker against evening light. Adrian approached with confident strides; his height seemed even more imposing from this angle than she remembered—Mara felt a brief twinge of self-consciousness under his penetrating stare but forced herself not to shift her gaze away as he came closer.
“Mara,” said Adrian, nodding at her—and then adding another slight nod in Jonah’s direction. “Join me here for dinner?”

segment:
A long face and a thick straight nose, with a hint of a moustache around the mouth. And bright eyes that didn’t seem to have decided how to look at her.
“Hi,” he said.
His voice was pleasant.
She crossed the room and sat down in a chair. The back of it faced the window.
“Hello,” she replied. “My name’s Mara.”
He nodded slightly but didn’t say anything else, or get up. She wasn’t sure what to expect from him.
The couch was quite far away. She could see only the surface details of his body; the way his shirt stretched across his shoulders, the curve of an elbow against the arm of the couch. The rest of him was hidden by the upholstery.
He hadn’t introduced himself yet, but she was sure it was going to happen soon. He wasn’t going to leave without knowing her name and that would mean knowing his own name too. And then they’d go on from there, talking and looking at each other until they both understood who they were here.
Maybe he knew things about her already, he had certainly seemed alert when she came into the room. But now that he knew that her name was Mara, she could be anyone. He would have to decide who she was again.
And if he thought anything of her arrival he kept it to himself.
